name: Protein Power Oatmeal
description: Creamy stovetop porridge with protein powder stirred through, topped with berries and toasted almonds for steady morning energy.
ingredients: 250 ml water or unsweetened almond milk
100 g (2/3 cup) mixed berries, fresh or frozen
steps: Put the oats, water or almond milk and a pinch of salt in a small pan.
Bring to a simmer and cook for 4-5 minutes, stirring often, until thick and creamy. (Microwave: 2-3 minutes on high in a large bowl, stirring halfway so it doesn't boil over.)
Take the pan off the heat and let it stand for 1 minute. Protein powder added to boiling porridge turns grainy.
Whisk the protein powder with 2-3 tbsp water or milk into a smooth paste, then stir it through the oats. Loosen with a splash more liquid if it's too thick.
Stir in the chia seeds, then top with the berries and chopped almonds.
tip: Good 2-3 hours before an easy or steady run. Before a hard session or race, leave out the chia and almonds to cut the fibre and fat so it sits lighter.

name: Greek Yogurt Parfait
description: Thick Greek yogurt layered with berries and crunchy high-fibre granola. Ready in five minutes and easy to pack in a jar.
steps: Stir the chia seeds into the yogurt and leave for 5 minutes to thicken slightly. This is optional, but it stops the seeds sticking in your teeth.
Spoon a third of the yogurt into a glass or jar, then add a layer of berries.
Repeat the layers, finishing with yogurt.
Scatter the granola on top just before eating so it stays crunchy, then drizzle with the honey.
tip: Protein-dense and quick, so it's a solid breakfast after an early easy run. For a packed breakfast, keep the granola in a separate bag.
storage: Assembled without the granola, it keeps for 24 hours in the fridge.

name: Veggie Scramble Wrap
description: Soft-scrambled eggs with peppers, spinach and melted cheddar, rolled in a warm wholewheat tortilla with avocado.
steps: Beat the eggs with the milk or water and a pinch of salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a non-stick pan over a medium heat. Soften the onion and pepper for 3 minutes, then add the spinach and stir until it wilts.

Turn the heat to medium-low and pour in the eggs. Stir slowly with a spatula, pulling the set egg from the edges into the middle. Take the pan off the heat after 2-3 minutes, while the eggs still look slightly glossy; they keep cooking.
Scatter the cheese over so it melts.
Warm the tortilla in a dry pan for 15 seconds each side, or 10 seconds in the microwave, so it folds without cracking.
Spoon the eggs down the centre and add the avocado. Fold in the ends, roll up tightly and cut in half on the diagonal.
tip: Wrapped in foil it travels well, so it makes a protein-rich refuel to eat after a morning run.

name: Overnight Protein Oats
description: No-cook oats soaked overnight with protein powder and chia. Make three jars on Sunday and breakfast is done until Wednesday.
steps: In a jar or container, whisk the protein powder into the milk until smooth. Added straight to dry oats, it clumps.
Stir in the oats and chia seeds. It will look runny; the oats and chia absorb the liquid overnight.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 6 hours, or overnight.
In the morning, stir well and loosen with a splash of milk if it's too thick. Top with the berries and walnuts.
Eat it cold, or microwave it for 60-90 seconds (without the berries) if you prefer it warm.
tip: The best breakfast for mornings when there's no time before an early run. The fibre is high, so eat it at least 2 hours before you head out.
storage: Keeps for 3 days in the fridge. Add the toppings on the day.

name: Breakfast Burrito
description: Softly scrambled eggs, cumin-spiced black beans, cheddar and salsa, rolled up and toasted to seal. Batch-make and freeze.
ingredients: 60 g tinned black beans, drained and rinsed
steps: Warm the beans in a small pan with the cumin and a splash of water for 2-3 minutes, lightly crushing about half of them with a fork so they hold together.
Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt. Heat the oil in a non-stick pan over a medium-low heat and softly scramble the eggs for about 2 minutes, taking them off while still a little wet.
Warm the tortilla in a dry pan for 15 seconds each side.
Spread the beans down the middle, then add the eggs, cheese, salsa and avocado.
Fold the bottom edge up over the filling, fold in the sides, then roll away from you to close.
Put it back in the hot pan seam-side down for 1 minute to seal and crisp.
tip: The beans add fibre, which makes this a great recovery breakfast. Before a hard run, eat it at least 3 hours ahead.
storage: Make four without the avocado, wrap each in foil and freeze. Reheat from frozen in the foil at 180°C for 25 minutes, or unwrap and microwave for 2 minutes.

name: Cottage Cheese Bowl
description: High-protein cottage cheese with juicy peaches, toasted pecans, flaxseed and a drizzle of honey.
ingredients: 150 g sliced peaches, fresh or tinned in juice and drained
steps: Spoon the cottage cheese into a bowl. If you dislike the curds, blitz it with a stick blender for 20 seconds for a smooth, yogurt-like base.
Top with the sliced peaches.
Toast the pecans in a dry pan for 2-3 minutes until fragrant, then roughly chop them and scatter them over.
Sprinkle with the flaxseed and finish with the honey.
tip: Cottage cheese is mostly casein, a slow-release protein, so this also works as a pre-bed snack on heavy training days.

name: Protein Pancakes
description: Fluffy oat-flour pancakes made in the blender with protein powder, stacked with berries and maple syrup.
steps: Blitz the oats in a blender for 30 seconds to a fine flour. Add the protein powder, baking powder and salt and pulse to mix.
Add the egg and milk and blend until smooth. Rest the batter for 5 minutes while the oats hydrate. It should drop slowly off a spoon; add a splash of milk if it's stiff.
Heat a non-stick pan over a medium-low heat and wipe it with a little butter. Protein batter burns quickly, so keep the heat lower than for normal pancakes.
Pour in 2-3 tbsp of batter per pancake. Cook for 1.5-2 minutes, until bubbles appear on the surface and the edges look set, then flip and cook for 1 minute more.
Stack them up, top with the berries and drizzle with the maple syrup.
tip: A weekend long-run breakfast: plenty of carbs plus protein. Eat it 2-3 hours before, or straight after as your recovery meal.

name: Tofu Scramble
description: Golden crumbled tofu with turmeric, nutritional yeast, peppers and spinach. A plant-based take on scrambled eggs, served on toast.
ingredients: Salt (or kala namak black salt) and black pepper
steps: Drain the tofu and press it between sheets of kitchen paper for a few minutes. Wet tofu steams instead of browning.
Heat the oil in a non-stick pan over a medium heat. Cook the onion and pepper for 3-4 minutes until soft.
Crumble the tofu into the pan in uneven, bite-size pieces. Cook for 4-5 minutes, turning occasionally, until lightly golden.
Sprinkle over the turmeric, nutritional yeast, a pinch of salt and some pepper. Kala namak gives an eggy flavour. Add the water or plant milk and stir until evenly yellow and creamy.
Fold in the spinach until just wilted and serve on the toast.
tip: Iron from the tofu and spinach, plus vitamin C from the pepper to help absorb it: useful if you run on a plant-based diet.

name: Egg Muffins
description: Baked egg cups packed with vegetables and cheddar. Make six on Sunday and grab two or three on the way out the door.
ingredients: 150 g diced vegetables (peppers, spinach, spring onion, mushrooms)
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C / 400°F). Grease 6 holes of a muffin tin well with oil, or use silicone cases; egg sticks badly to bare metal.
Divide the vegetables and half the cheese between the holes.
Whisk the eggs with the milk, salt and plenty of pepper, then pour the mixture over the vegetables until each hole is three-quarters full.
Top with the remaining cheese and bake for 18-20 minutes, until puffed and just set in the centre. A knife pushed into the middle should come out clean.
Cool in the tin for 5 minutes, then run a knife around each one to release it.
tip: Low in carbs on their own. On a training day, pair them with toast or fruit so you actually refuel.
storage: Keeps for 4 days in the fridge or a month in the freezer. Reheat for 30-40 seconds in the microwave.

name: Chia Seed Pudding
description: Thick vanilla chia pudding boosted with protein powder and topped with berries. Five minutes tonight, breakfast tomorrow.
steps: In a jar, whisk the protein powder into the milk until completely smooth.
Add the chia seeds and maple syrup and whisk for 30 seconds.
Leave it for 5 minutes, then whisk again. The second stir breaks up the clumps that form as the seeds start to swell.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or overnight, until thick and spoonable.
Stir, loosen with a splash of milk if needed, and top with the berries.
tip: Very high in fibre, which makes it ideal on a rest or easy day. Skip it on the morning of a race or a hard session.
storage: Keeps for 4 days in the fridge.

name: Spinach and Feta Omelette
description: A soft, folded omelette filled with wilted spinach, salty feta and tomatoes. On the table in ten minutes.
steps: Heat the oil in a non-stick frying pan over a medium heat. Add the spinach and stir for 1-2 minutes until wilted, then tip it onto a plate and squeeze out any water.
Whisk the eggs with the milk, a small pinch of salt (feta is salty) and some pepper.
Pour the eggs into the same pan. As the base sets, push the cooked edges towards the centre with a spatula and tilt the pan so raw egg runs underneath. This takes 2-3 minutes.
When the top is almost set but still slightly moist, scatter the spinach, feta and tomatoes over one half.
Fold the other half over the filling, cook for 1 minute more, then slide it onto a plate.
tip: High protein, but almost no carbs. Add a slice or two of toast if you're training later that day.

name: Smoked Salmon Bagel
description: A toasted wholegrain bagel with cream cheese, smoked salmon, capers, red onion and dill. The classic weekend brunch.
ingredients: A few thin slices of red onion
steps: Split the bagel and toast it until golden and crisp.
Spread the cream cheese over both halves.
Drape the smoked salmon over the bottom half, then add the red onion, capers and a few sprigs of dill.
Squeeze over the lemon, grind over black pepper and put the top on.
tip: Salmon brings omega-3s and quality protein. It makes a good post-long-run brunch; if you're eating it before a run, halve the cream cheese.

name: Avocado Toast with Everything Seasoning
description: Lemony smashed avocado on wholegrain toast with a crunchy homemade everything-bagel seasoning.
ingredients: 1 tsp everything-bagel seasoning (or mix sesame seeds, poppy seeds, dried garlic, dried onion and flaky salt)
steps: Toast the bread until golden and crisp.
Mash the avocado with the lemon juice, salt and pepper, leaving it slightly chunky.
Spread it thickly over the toast.
Sprinkle generously with the everything seasoning and red pepper flakes, then top with the microgreens.
tip: On its own it's light on protein. Adding two sliced boiled eggs brings about 150 kcal and 12 g protein, which turns it into a proper post-run breakfast.

name: Savory Oatmeal Bowl
description: Oats cooked in stock with nutritional yeast and cheddar, topped with golden mushrooms and a fried egg. Porridge, but savoury.
steps: Bring the stock to the boil in a small pan. Stir in the oats, turn the heat down and simmer for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until creamy.
Meanwhile, heat the oil in a frying pan over a medium-high heat and cook the mushrooms for 4-5 minutes until golden. Push them to one side and fry the egg in the same pan.
Stir the nutritional yeast and half the cheese into the oats and season with pepper.
Tip into a bowl, top with the mushrooms, egg, remaining cheese and chives.
tip: A savoury change when sweet breakfasts get old in a big training block. The salty stock also helps replace sodium after a sweaty morning run.

name: Berry Protein Smoothie Bowl
description: A spoon-thick berry and banana smoothie bowl with Greek yogurt and protein, topped with granola, chia and fresh fruit.
ingredients: 60 ml almond milk, plus extra if needed
steps: Put the frozen banana, frozen berries, yogurt, protein powder and 60 ml of milk in a blender.
Pulse, then blend, stopping to scrape down the sides. Keep it thick: add more milk only 1 tbsp at a time, and only if the blades can't move.
Scoop it into a chilled bowl.
Top with the granola, chia seeds and fresh berries, and eat straight away before it melts.
tip: Frozen banana is what makes it thick enough to eat with a spoon, so freeze ripe bananas in chunks. A strong recovery breakfast after a morning session.

name: Pre-Run Banana and Honey Toast
description: White toast with a thin smear of peanut butter, sliced banana, honey and a pinch of salt. Quick-digesting fuel for race mornings.
ingredients: 2 slices white bread or white sourdough
steps: Toast the bread lightly.
Spread a very thin layer of peanut butter, if using.
Slice the banana over the toast.
Drizzle with the honey and finish with a pinch of flaky salt.
tip: Eat it 60-90 minutes before a long run or race. The white bread is deliberate: less fibre means less gut trouble once you start running. Try it before a long training run first.

name: Shakshuka with Chickpeas
description: Eggs poached in a smoky spiced tomato and chickpea sauce, finished with feta and herbs. A brunch you eat straight from the pan.
steps: Heat the oil in a wide frying pan that has a lid, over a medium heat. Cook the onion and pepper for 6-8 minutes until soft and sweet.
Add the garlic, cumin, paprika and chilli flakes and stir for 1 minute until fragrant.
Tip in the tomatoes and chickpeas, season, and simmer for 8-10 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick enough that a spoon leaves a trail.
Make 4 wells in the sauce with the back of a spoon and crack an egg into each.
Cover and cook on a low heat for 5-7 minutes, until the whites are set but the yolks are still runny.
Crumble over the feta, scatter with herbs and serve from the pan with bread for dipping.
tip: A weekend brunch after the long run: protein from the eggs and chickpeas, carbs from the bread, and potassium from the tomatoes.

name: Apple Cinnamon Bircher Muesli
description: Swiss-style soaked oats with grated apple, yogurt, raisins and cinnamon, topped with toasted hazelnuts.
steps: Coarsely grate three-quarters of the apple, skin on, into a bowl and toss with the lemon juice so it doesn't brown.
Add the oats, yogurt, milk, raisins and cinnamon and stir well.
Cover and refrigerate overnight, or for at least 4 hours.
In the morning, loosen with a splash of milk. Divide between two bowls and top with the rest of the apple, cut into matchsticks, the hazelnuts and the honey.
tip: Soaked oats are gentler on the stomach than dry muesli. Make it the night before a morning run.
storage: Keeps for 2 days in the fridge.

name: Blueberry Baked Oats
description: Banana-sweetened oats baked with juicy blueberries until golden and cake-like. Serve warm with yogurt.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C / 400°F).
Mash the banana in a small baking dish (about 20 x 15 cm), then whisk in the egg, milk, maple syrup, cinnamon, baking powder and salt.
Stir in the oats, then fold through the blueberries.
Bake for 25 minutes, until golden and just firm in the middle.
Rest for 5 minutes, then serve with the yogurt.
tip: Good fuel for a long run: eat it 2-3 hours before you set off, or after as your recovery meal.
storage: Keeps for 3 days in the fridge. Reheat a portion for 1 minute in the microwave.

name: Sweet Potato and Egg Breakfast Hash
description: Crisp-edged sweet potato with peppers, onion and smoked paprika, with eggs cooked into the pan. Naturally gluten-free.
ingredients: 200 g sweet potato, cut into 1.5 cm cubes
steps: Put the sweet potato in a bowl with 1 tbsp water, cover and microwave for 3 minutes to par-cook it. This halves the time in the pan.
Heat the oil in a non-stick frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add the sweet potato in a single layer and leave it undisturbed for 4 minutes to brown.
Add the onion, pepper and paprika and cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until everything is tender and crisp at the edges. Stir in the spinach until it wilts.
Make two wells, crack in the eggs, cover the pan and cook for 3-4 minutes until the whites are set.
Season and scatter with chives.
tip: Gluten-free carbs for long-run weekends. Add a slice of ham or a sausage for more protein.

name: Sweet Rice Porridge with Maple and Banana
description: Cooked rice simmered in milk with cinnamon until creamy, sweetened with maple and topped with banana. Gentle, carb-rich race-morning food.
ingredients: 150 g cooked white rice (leftover, or a microwave pouch)
steps: Put the rice, milk, salt and cinnamon in a small pan.
Simmer for 6-8 minutes, stirring often, until thick and creamy.
Stir in the maple syrup.
Top with the banana, or mash half of it into the porridge if you like it sweeter.
tip: One of the gentlest pre-race breakfasts there is: lots of carbohydrate and almost no fibre. Eat it 2-3 hours before the start. If you use leftover rice, it must have been cooled quickly and refrigerated within an hour.

name: Turkish Eggs with Garlic Yogurt
description: Soft poached eggs on cool garlicky yogurt with a sizzling paprika butter and dill (cilbir). Serve with toasted sourdough.
ingredients: 1/2 tsp Aleppo pepper or sweet paprika
steps: Mix the yogurt with the garlic and a pinch of salt. Spread it in a shallow bowl and let it come up towards room temperature while you cook; cold yogurt chills the eggs.
Bring a deep pan of water to a bare simmer and add the vinegar. Crack each egg into a cup. Stir the water into a gentle whirlpool and slide the eggs in one at a time.
Poach for 3 minutes for runny yolks, then lift out with a slotted spoon onto kitchen paper.
Melt the butter in a small pan until foaming, take it off the heat and stir in the Aleppo pepper and cumin.
Sit the eggs on the yogurt, spoon over the spiced butter, scatter with dill and serve with the toast.
tip: More than 30 g of protein with very little effort: a restaurant-style recovery brunch.

name: Smoked Salmon Scrambled Eggs on Rye
description: Slow-cooked creamy scrambled eggs folded with smoked salmon and chives, piled onto toasted rye.
ingredients: 50 g smoked salmon, cut into strips
steps: Beat the eggs with the milk and plenty of black pepper. Skip the salt; the salmon is salty.
Put the rye in the toaster.
Melt the butter in a non-stick pan over a low heat. Add the eggs and stir constantly with a spatula for 3-4 minutes, until they form soft, creamy curds.
Take the pan off the heat and fold in the salmon and chives.
Pile onto the toast and finish with a squeeze of lemon.
tip: Low and slow is the secret to creamy eggs. The rye adds fibre and releases its carbs more slowly, which suits a rest-day breakfast.
